messages:
vika: Heads-up: a customer pasted our Go generator snippet into an HTTP handler and hit goroutine growth. The quickstart creates streams with context.Background() so cancels never propagate.

owen: Yikes. Quick fix for docs: show using the request ctx (r.Context()) or context.WithTimeout derived from it, and call `defer gen.Close()` immediately after creating the stream.

vika: Example I'd drop in:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()
// client is long-lived; pass ctx into calls
gen := client.Generator(ctx, req)
defer gen.Close()
for gen.Next() { token := gen.Token(); _ = token }
```
Keep it short and copy-pastable.

rita: There's a companion bug in our retry helper: we'll sleep during backoff without observing ctx.Done(), which keeps goroutines alive even after cancel. I pushed a tiny change to use `time.NewTimer` + `select` on `timer.C` and `ctx.Done()`.

sam: Filed issue #3652 with a small repro and a pprof showing stacks. I also added a minimal sample-app that reproduces the leak when you use Background(). Repo: https://github.com/redwood/sample-go-gen-leak

owen: Can we add a CI test that asserts no goroutine leak? Plan: record baseline goroutines, start a generator with a cancellable ctx, cancel, wait ~100ms, then assert goroutine count <= baseline + epsilon. Add flakiness guard.

docbot: CI: build 9014 on branch fix/go-gen-ctx-cancel passed :white_check_mark: (retry helper + test added)

vika: Nice. Action items: 1) docs PR to update quickstart and add a short sidebar "use request context, not Background()", 2) merge retry fix, 3) add leak-smoke test to CI, 4) track API parity RFC for stream naming (Close vs CloseStream).

rita: One more ergonomics thought: we call `gen.Close()` in examples but some streams are `CloseStream()` elsewhere. Standardize to `Close()` to reduce cognitive load. I'll open an RFC outlining the compatibility plan.

sam: Thanks everyone. I'll update the sample-app repro with the new test and link it in the issue so support can point customers to a reproducible case.
